persona.name: Debbie Kowalchuk
persona.background: Anglophone, 14 in 1972, Ukrainian-Canadian father works for the CPR, mother a hospital clerk. Music came from CHAB 800 Moose Jaw and CKCK Regina on a transistor radio, 45s from Woolworths, CTV's The Tommy Hunter Show and Don Messer reruns with her parents, school sock hops, community-hall wedding dances with old-time and polka bands.

seeds.song: Gordon Lightfoot - If You Could Read My Mind

CA1972A.wouldSay: Oh, Heart of Gold, that was all over CHAB that winter. But Snowbird and American Woman, that's grade six, not grade nine. This is every Canadian song anybody remembers from the early seventies, not my 1972.
missing: The Guess Who - Runnin' Back to Saskatoon, 1972
April Wine - You Could Have Been a Lady, 1972
A Foot in Coldwater - (Make Me Do) Anything You Want, 1972
CA1972A.fake: Only Heart of Gold and Crocodile Rock belong to 1972; the other four are the 1970-71 Canadian standards any outsider would pick, each one or two years stale (inside the three-year rule, but it reads as a greatest-hits list).
CA1972A.missingScene: Country, which was half of Prairie listening (Tommy Hunter, Stompin' Tom, Family Brown, Charley Pride on tour); the 1972 CanCon rock bands on AM; the US/UK top 40 that still filled most of the dial (American Pie, Alone Again, Brandy); nothing in French.

seeds.song: Frank Mills - Love Me, Love Me Love
Roberta Flack - The First Time Ever I Saw Your Face
April Wine - You Could Have Been a Lady
The Guess Who - Runnin' Back to Saskatoon

CA1972B.wouldSay: American Pie, we sang every verse on the school bus. Frank Mills! The Bells! And Runnin' Back to Saskatoon, 'Moose Jaw, Broadview, Moosomin too', they played that every hour at home. This is exactly the radio in our kitchen.
missing: A Foot in Coldwater - (Make Me Do) Anything You Want, 1972
Joni Mitchell - You Turn Me On, I'm a Radio, 1972
Looking Glass - Brandy (You're a Fine Girl), 1972
CA1972B.fake: Little; the one French track never reached Prairie radio (I am also unsure Mon cœur was Pagliaro's 1972 hit rather than J'entends frapper), and Sweet City Woman and Stay Awhile are 1971.
CA1972B.missingScene: Prairie country beyond one Stompin' Tom novelty (Tommy Hunter show regulars, Family Brown, Dick Damron); old-time and polka dance bands at hall weddings; harder rock the older kids played (Deep Purple, Alice Cooper - School's Out).

persona.name: Sylvie Gauthier
persona.background: Francophone, 15 in 1976, father at the Wayagamack paper mill, mother at home, three siblings. Music came from CHLN and CJMS/CKAC on AM, CHOM-FM and the new CKOI-FM when the signal held, her older brother's Harmonium and Beau Dommage LPs, Radio-Canada and Tele-Metropole variety shows, the Saint-Jean shows of 1975-76, polyvalente dances with disco, and the Olympic summer on TV.

seeds.song: Gordon Lightfoot - The Wreck of the Edmund Fitzgerald
Rod Stewart - Tonight's the Night (Gonna Be Alright)
April Wine - The Whole World's Goin' Crazy
Rick Dees & His Cast of Idiots - Disco Duck
Beau Dommage - Le blues d'la métropole
Carroll Baker - One Night of Cheatin'
Elton John & Kiki Dee - Don't Go Breaking My Heart
Patsy Gallant - From New York to L.A.
Boule Noire - Aimes-tu la vie comme moi?

CA1976A.wouldSay: Roxy Roller? Lightfoot? C'est la radio de Toronto, ca. Ah, Andre Gagnon, Wow, la oui, on dansait la-dessus. Beau Dommage, enfin. But why is Patsy Gallant singing in English, chez nous c'etait Mon pays.
missing: Robert Charlebois - Je reviendrai à Montréal, 1976
Ginette Reno - Un peu plus haut, un peu plus loin, 1975-76
CA1976A.fake: It is the 1976 RPM (English-Canadian) chart with three Quebec tracks dropped in; the first five songs give a francophone nothing in French, and English-Canadian country and CanCon pop (Carroll Baker, Charity Brown, Wednesday, Burton Cummings) never played on our stations.
CA1976A.missingScene: The whole 1976 Quebec chanson and prog wave (Harmonium's L'Heptade, Charlebois, Dufresne, Ferland, Seguin, Octobre, Vigneault, the Saint-Jean and 1 fois 5 shows), French imports that were huge (Dassin, Fugain, Dave), Quebec country-western (Willie Lamothe, Paul Brunelle), and Montreal disco in French (Nanette Workman, Toulouse). Unsure whether the Boule Noire single is 1976 or 1978.

persona.name: Sylvie Gauthier

seeds.song: Gordon Lightfoot - The Wreck of the Edmund Fitzgerald
Robert Charlebois - Je reviendrai à Montréal
Beau Dommage - La complainte du phoque en Alaska

CA1976B.wouldSay: Je reviendrai a Montreal, ah oui, c'etait l'hiver 76. Pour un instant, mon frere jouait ca a la guitare tous les soirs. Le phoque en Alaska, tout le monde la savait par coeur. Hotel California, non, ca c'est secondaire quatre, 1977.
missing: Beau Dommage - Le blues d'la métropole, 1975
Ginette Reno - Un peu plus haut, un peu plus loin, 1975-76
Patsy Gallant - Mon pays (From New York to L.A.), 1976
CA1976B.fake: Pour un instant and Le phoque are 1974 songs, still everywhere but not that year's hits (two years early, inside the rule), and Hotel California only became a hit in 1977; the opener is English Canada's song, not ours.
CA1976B.missingScene: Disco, which ran Montreal and every polyvalente dance in 1976 (Gagnon, Gallant, Boule Noire, Toulouse, Nanette Workman); French imports (Dassin, Fugain); Quebec country-western and kitchen-party music; for an anglophone listener the seeds have almost no English-Canadian 1976 (Sweeney Todd, April Wine, Burton Cummings, Heart).

persona.name: Jennifer MacLeod
persona.background: Anglophone, 14 in 1984, father at General Electric, mother a school secretary. Music came from CHUM 1050 and CFTR 680 out of Toronto, local CKPT, Q107 from her older brother's room, CBC's Video Hits with Samantha Taylor, CITY-TV's Toronto Rocks, MuchMusic once cable carried it in the fall, taped-off-the-radio cassettes and school dances.

seeds.song: Men Without Hats - The Safety Dance
Wham! - Wake Me Up Before You Go-Go

CA1984A.wouldSay: Summer of '69 wasn't on the radio till the next summer, in '84 it was Run to You. Rise Up and Safety Dance were grade seven, 1983. Sunglasses at Night, okay, now that's the grade eight dance. Who's the French girl? Nobody in Peterborough had heard of Celine Dion.
CA1984A.fake: A best-of-the-Canadian-eighties list rather than 1984: the opener was a 1985 single, two more are 1983 hits, and the Celine Dion track never crossed out of Quebec.
CA1984A.missingScene: Toronto new wave and the CFNY sound (Platinum Blonde, Spoons, Pukka Orchestra, Images in Vogue, Jane Siberry), Ontario hard rock (Rush, Triumph, Helix, Kim Mitchell), and the giant foreign 1984 (Prince, Springsteen, Van Halen, Cyndi Lauper, Ghostbusters).

seeds.song: Stevie Wonder - I Just Called to Say I Love You
The Pukka Orchestra - Listen to the Radio
Phil Collins - Against All Odds (Take a Look at Me Now)
Tina Turner - What's Love Got to Do with It
Anne Murray & Dave Loggins - Nobody Loves Me Like You Do
The Parachute Club - At the Feet of the Moon
Bruce Cockburn - Lovers in a Dangerous Time

CA1984B.wouldSay: Sunglasses at Night, New Girl Now, that's Video Hits after school. Listen to the Radio! I haven't heard that since CFTR. Go for Soda, my brother wore that tape out. This is grade eight, exactly.
missing: Jane Siberry - Mimi on the Beach, 1984
CA1984B.fake: Only the three Quebec tracks, which an Ontario kid never heard (and I am unsure all three are 1984 releases); the rest is right, though Let It Go really peaked in early 1985.
CA1984B.missingScene: Platinum Blonde and the Toronto new-wave video bands, hard rock and metal for the boys (Helix, Triumph, Rush, Van Halen, Twisted Sister), and the Prince/Springsteen/Lauper/Culture Club imports that dominated CHUM.

persona.name: Kristina Lindqvist
persona.background: Born in Canada to parents who emigrated from Varmland in 1968; father a millwright, mother a care aide; Swedish at home, Lucia and midsummer with the Swedish community, parents' ABBA and Sven-Ingvars LPs. Her own music, age 15: LG73 (CKLG) and CFOX on the radio, MuchMusic, CBC's Good Rockin' Tonite, cassettes from A&B Sound, high-school dances, and pride when Europe's The Final Countdown was on Canadian radio.

seeds.song: Glass Tiger - Don't Forget Me (When I'm Gone)
Whitney Houston - I Wanna Dance with Somebody (Who Loves Me)
Bon Jovi - Livin' on a Prayer

CA1988A.wouldSay: Mitsou, okay, that video was on Much. But Patio Lanterns and Don't Forget Me are Expo summer, 1986, I was in grade seven. Summer of '69 is older still. I know every one of these, but none of it is grade ten.
missing: Tom Cochrane & Red Rider - Big League, 1988
Barney Bentall and the Legendary Hearts - Something to Live For, 1988
Men Without Hats - Pop Goes the World, 1987-88
CA1988A.fake: Five of six seeds are 1984-87 hits; only Mitsou is from 1988, so it plays as a generic mid-eighties Canada mix rather than the year asked for.
CA1988A.missingScene: The Vancouver/West Coast scene of 1988 (Colin James, Barney Bentall, 54-40, Grapes of Wrath, Paul Janz), Much dance-pop (Candi, Sway, Rick Astley, Kylie), hair metal and Guns N' Roses, and for a Scandinavian household nothing of what came from home (Europe; Roxette only arrived in 1989).

CA1988B.wouldSay: I'm Still Searching, yes, that was LG73 all spring. Then somebody in French I don't know. Billy Ocean, Rick Astley, Pop Goes the World, okay, that's the grade ten dance. Big League still gets me.
missing: Barney Bentall and the Legendary Hearts - Something to Live For, 1988
Candi - Dancing Under a Latin Moon, 1988
The Jeff Healey Band - Angel Eyes, 1988

CA1988B.fake: The second song is a Quebec-only Celine Dion track no BC teenager knew in 1988, and with the Simards and Family Brown it reads like a national chart digest rather than one person's radio.
CA1988B.missingScene: Vancouver's own 1988 (Colin James, Barney Bentall, 54-40, Grapes of Wrath, Skinny Puppy for the alternative kids), hard rock and hair metal on CFOX (Def Leppard, GN'R, Bon Jovi's New Jersey), George Michael/INXS/U2, and early hip-hop arriving on Much.
